title: Proton pump inhibitors and risk of incident CKD and progression to ESRD
authors: Xie Y, Bowe B, Li T, Xian H, Balasubramanian S, Al-Aly Z
journal: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology
population: US Department of Veterans Affairs new users of PPIs (n = 173,321) or H2-receptor antagonists (n = 20,270)
funder: Not read: the PubMed Central record holds a PDF only, which could not be retrieved, and the publisher page refused access.
result: Against H2-receptor antagonist users, PPI users had higher risk of incident eGFR below 60 mL/min/1.73 m2 (HR 1.22, 95% CI 1.18 to 1.26), incident CKD (1.28, 1.23 to 1.34), doubling of serum creatinine (1.53, 1.42 to 1.65), eGFR decline above 30% (1.32, 1.28 to 1.37) and end-stage renal disease (1.96, 1.21 to 3.18), with graded association by duration of exposure from 31 to 720 days.
